claims.text: The retention of a stable, coherent, slow-growing oxide above 900 °C is controlled by the uniformity of Cr and X distribution in the solid solution.
Cr and Al form passivating oxides in CrFeCoNiAl-type alloys.
A homogeneous single-phase solid solution produces balanced, controlled outward diffusion of Cr and X relative to oxygen ingress.
Balanced outward diffusion in a homogeneous alloy produces a continuous, adherent oxide with minimal internal stress.
Al2O3 will dominate the protective scale when X is Al.
Al2O3 scales grow more slowly and are more stable than chromia scales.
Phase boundaries and segregation in multiphase alloys provide enhanced diffusion paths that accelerate differential oxide growth.
Non-uniform oxide growth causes stress accumulation that leads to cracking or spallation.
Si and Mn do not form oxides that are comparably slow-growing and stable to Al2O3 in these alloys.
Single-phase CrFeCoNiAl will develop a thin, slowly growing, coherent, Al2O3-rich scale that persists without cracking.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiMn will develop thicker, less uniform scales prone to cracking or spallation.
Multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys will develop thicker, less uniform scales prone to cracking or spallation than homogeneous single-phase variants.
The comparison will independently vary X among Al, Si, and Mn and vary the material state between homogeneous single-phase and multiphase conditions.
Samples will be exposed isothermally at approximately 925 °C for 100 hours under identical atmospheric and surface conditions.
Oxide thickness, growth kinetics, morphology, cracking, spallation, composition, and phase identity will be measured by gravimetry, SEM, XRD, and EDS.
Multiphase variants and Si- or Mn-containing variants tested under the same conditions constitute the baseline.
The hypothesis is limited to temperatures above 900 °C and atmospheres with sufficient oxidizing potential.

The mechanism is falsified if single-phase Al-containing alloys are not significantly thinner, more coherent, and slower-growing than both Si/Mn alloys and multiphase variants, or if oxide stability does not correlate with microstructural homogeneity.
